records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool
records.summary: Personally designed and built an operational dispatch reconciliation tool using a Python parser and SQL checks. Gathered requirements from warehouse supervisors, explained validation failures, and used Git and PostgreSQL. Operators compared an overnight spreadsheet with a daily export; the tool surfaced understandable exceptions, including late-file warnings and visible empty rows. Supervisors made final dispatch decisions.

decisions.reason: The name, profile description, and listed professional-use and employment denials are supported by the source.
The role, employer, dates, tool-building and training summary, and linked skills and achievements are supported. The source also explicitly corrects the initially guessed start year to 2021.

The source says operators preferred a visible warning when a source file arrived late, but does not establish that the tool actually surfaced late-file warnings. The project summary presents that preference as implemented functionality.
The time reduction, six weekly runs, team attribution, Ada’s parser-and-checks contribution, and clarification that delivery speed was not measured are supported.
The source supports the training of 12 coworkers in two workshops and the handbook. It also says exact workshop dates are unknown, and the record leaves them blank.
The source says Ada wrote the Python parser herself, supporting the skill and its summary.
The source says Ada wrote the SQL checks herself, supporting the skill and its summary.
The source identifies PostgreSQL as the production database, in the context of Dispatch Loom.
The source says Ada used Git for version control and explicitly places Git in the Collaboration skill category.
The source supports training dispatch coworkers and writing the plain-language handbook; the Collaboration category is also explicitly stated.
The degree, institution, and dates match the source.
The source explicitly qualifies this as a fictional certificate. The record presents it as an ordinary earned credential without preserving that material qualification.
